dialog.body: City of Newport Finance Department, this is Janet Whitcomb. How may I help you?
Hi, yes, hello. Um, my name is Walter Almy. I got two parking tickets and I don't understand it, and I just want to make sure I'm doing this right. Is it okay if I ask you about them?
Certainly, Mr. Almy. Do you have the ticket numbers in front of you?

I do, I do. They're both stuck to, well, I have them here. But the thing is, they're the same place, same day. Two tickets. Same spot, same street, a few hours apart. Is that, can they do that? Is that allowed?
It can happen, yes. If a vehicle remains in a restricted space, an officer may issue a second citation later in the day. Let me look them up. Could you read me the first ticket number?
Okay, uh, it's one-one-four-eight-two-six. And the other one is one-one-four-nine-oh-three. Did I say that right? I can say it again.

One-one-four-eight-two-six and one-one-four-nine-oh-three. Thank you. [pause] I have both here. They were issued Friday, the nineteenth, on the same block, one in the late morning and one in the afternoon.

Right, right, that's them. But I only parked once. I parked in the morning and I came back and the car was where I left it. So how is that two? I mean, is it okay to, can I fight one of them? Or both?
You may appeal either or both. The appeal has to be submitted in writing, and each citation is handled separately.
In writing. Okay. Like a letter? Or is there a form? I'm sorry, I'm not good with this. Do I send one letter for two tickets or two letters, is that okay?
I would recommend one appeal per citation, each referencing its own ticket number. There is an appeal form, and you can pick it up at City Hall or I can mail one to you.

Mail would be good. Wait, do you need my address for that? Because I thought, well, okay. I'm on a flip phone, still, I like it, so I can't just look it up on the, you know, the internet on it. That's why I'm calling.
I understand. I can mail it, but I will need your mailing address, and the plate number on the vehicle so I can confirm the record.
Oh. Um. Hold on, I thought you said you didn't need the address. No, wait, you said you did. Okay. Actually, can I just come pick it up? Is that okay? Then I don't have to say it all over the phone.
That is perfectly fine. The form is available at the counter during regular hours. Tomorrow is Tuesday, and we are open until the usual closing time.

Okay, good. And then how long does the appeal take? Like once I turn it in, how long till I know? Because I don't want it to, the fines, I don't want them to go up while I wait. Is that okay, will they go up?

Review generally takes a few weeks. I would not want to give you a precise date. As to the fine, I would ask that you bring the form in promptly, and the clerk at the counter can tell you how the due date is treated while an appeal is pending.
A few weeks. Okay. So a few weeks, and the counter will tell me about the, the late part. And that's okay, I just come in and ask?
Yes, that is correct. Bring both ticket numbers and your vehicle registration. If you have any photographs of where you parked, include those with the form.
I have a picture, I think. My neighbor, no, well, I'll look. Registration and ticket numbers and a picture. Did I get that right? I don't want to forget one.
You have it exactly right, Mr. Almy.
Okay. Thank you. Thank you very much. I really appreciate it. Sorry for all the questions.
No trouble at all. Have a good afternoon.
